up.name: OKTA INC CLASS A

See the wiki entry at wiki/companies/OKTA (overview, Q1 FY27 transcript, thesis).
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q2 FY27 beat ($805M rev, $1.05 adj EPS) plus FY27 raise sent shares up 29% on Aug 27.

up.name: SALESFORCE INC
up.company_description: Salesforce is an Information Technology application-software company that sells cloud CRM, industry clouds, and AI-agent subscriptions (Agentforce) to enterprises.
bullets: Aug 26 Q2 FY27: revenue $11.35B (+11% YoY) vs ~$11.32B; cRPO $33.5B (+14% CC, fastest bookings in four years); RPO $66.3B (+11%). Subscription and support $10.8B (+12%), including $440M Informatica.
Adj EPS $5.90 vs $3.27 Street, inflated by a $2.6B mark-to-market on Anthropic (May round valued it at $965B); ex-gain adj EPS ~$3.37. GAAP NI $3.53B / $4.29. FCF $1.10B (+81% YoY).

Agentforce ARR >$1.5B (+240% YoY); Agentforce + Data 360 ARR ~$3.9B (+210%). 3.2B agentic work units in Q2 (+97% QoQ). Launched Claudeforce with Anthropic (Salesforce-in-Claude plugin; open beta Sep-26).

Raised FY27 revenue to $46.1–$46.4B (+$200M, +$300M CC): $100M organic Agentforce/Data 360/Slack, $200M pending Contentful and Fin. Q3 revenue $11.42–$11.50B. Aug 27: +22.6% to $252.05 on 55M shares — largest daily jump since 2020.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q2 FY27 $11.35B rev, $5.90 adj EPS, Agentforce ARR $1.5B and Claudeforce; stock +23% Aug 27.

up.name: GAP INC
up.company_description: Gap Inc is a Consumer Discretionary apparel retailer that sells clothing through Old Navy, Gap, Banana Republic, and Athleta stores and e-commerce.
bullets: Aug 27 AMC (quarter ended Aug 1): net sales $3.651B (−2% YoY) vs ~$3.69B; comps −1%. Adj EPS $0.52 vs ~$0.48–$0.50. GAAP EPS $1.38 / NI $501M, inflated by a $417M net IEEPA tariff recovery (received $95M refunds + $5M interest in-quarter).
Gap brand comps +10% (11th straight quarter; sales $844M +9%) vs ~8.8% LSEG. Banana Republic comps +3%. Old Navy sales $2.1B, comps −4% (first negative since Q2 2023); Athleta comps −12%.

Raised FY26 adj EPS to $2.35–$2.45 from $2.30–$2.40; trimmed sales growth to +1–1.5% from +1–2% (Old Navy comps now flat to −1%). Named Michael Francis Old Navy CEO effective Nov 2, succeeding Haio Barbeito.
Aug 28 shares +12.9% to $23.48 (intraday high $25.80) on ~23M volume vs ~8M average as the Gap-brand print and EPS raise outweighed the Old Navy miss. BTIG lifted PT to $27 from $26.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q2 adj EPS $0.52 beat, Gap-brand comps +10%, FY26 EPS raise to $2.35–$2.45; stock +13% Aug 28.

up.name: LIBERTY BROADBAND CORP SERIES A
up.company_description: Liberty Broadband is a Communication Services Charter tracking stock that converted into Charter shares; it previously held CHTR equity plus Alaska broadband GCI.
bullets: Aug 19–20: two-step merger into Charter closed; each LBRDA share converted into 0.236 CHTR Class A (cash for fractionals). Nasdaq delisting of LBRDA/LBRDK/LBRDP requested Aug 20 (Form 25).
Same day Charter closed the $34.5B Cox Communications deal: ~37M customers across 45 states; issued ~46M-share equivalent to Cox Enterprises (~26% of combined) and assumed ~$12B Cox debt.

Liberty math: Charter retired 38.6M CHTR shares held by Liberty, issued ~33.9M new shares to LBRD holders (net −4.7M), and assumed ~$840M Liberty net debt plus $180M preferred. Last LBRDA print Aug 19 was $35.99 (implied ~0.236 × CHTR in the $150s).

The +17% 5d print is the close/conversion re-rating into CHTR as Cox closed (CHTR fell 4.7% Aug 20 then recovered). Background: Liberty Q2 (Jun 30) revenue $261M flat, $3.0B Charter-stake impairment, GAAP loss $2.13B; GCI had already been spun.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Charter closed Liberty Broadband Aug 19–20; each share became 0.236 CHTR as the $34.5B Cox deal also closed.

up.name: LIBERTY BROADBAND CORP SERIES C
up.company_description: Liberty Broadband Series C is the non-voting twin of LBRDA, a Communication Services Charter tracking stock that converted into the same 0.236 CHTR package.
bullets: Same catalyst as LBRDA: Aug 19–20 two-step merger into Charter; each LBRDK share converted into 0.236 CHTR Class A with cash for fractionals; Nasdaq delisting requested Aug 20.

Last LBRDK print Aug 19 was $36.13 (inactive thereafter). Citi had a $42 PT on Aug 14. The +17% 5d move matches LBRDA and is the conversion-into-CHTR plus Cox-close re-rating, not a separate operating print.
Q2 Liberty (Jun 30) revenue $261M flat, Adjusted OIBDA −11%, $3.0B impairment on the Charter stake and GAAP loss $2.13B; GCI Alaska was spun before close and was not in the Charter package.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Same as LBRDA: Aug 19–20 Charter merger at 0.236 CHTR per share, concurrent with the $34.5B Cox close.

See the wiki entry for Elastic’s platform, April 30 fiscal year, and prior-quarter thesis.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 27 Q1 FY27 beat-and-raise: $478M revenue (+15%), $0.70 adj. EPS vs $0.58, FY27 guide lifted.

up.name: CONCENTRIX CORP
up.company_description: Concentrix is an Industrials-sector CX/BPO provider that designs and runs customer-experience, digital operations, and AI orchestration (iX) services for large enterprises.
bullets: [2026-08-21→08-28] No company print in-window (next earnings Sep 24). Stock ground from $25.40 on Aug 21 to ~$29.41, a ~16% five-day gain after an $19.12 52-week low earlier this year.

[2026-08-26/27] Sector AI-disruption fears eased after Salesforce’s blowout and CrowdStrike’s record ARR print; CNXC had been a high-beta AI-killed BPO name (FY26 CC growth guided only 0.25–1.25% after Q2).

[2026-08-25] Short interest 10.57M shares, ~20% of float and 10.6 days to cover — a squeeze-prone setup as the name rebounded. ~$1.8B market cap vs ~$10B TTM revenue; ~5% dividend ($1.44) after the Jul 24 ex-date.
Q2 FY26 (Jun 29) still frames the story: iX Suite deal count +400% YoY, targeting >$120M ARR, record $242M adj. FCF; $200M of 6.650% notes were due August 2026.
See the wiki entry for Concentrix’s CX/iX model and Q2 FY26 ingest.
up.ten_day_catalyst: No company news in-window; grind-up as SaaS AI-disruption fears eased after CRM/CRWD, with ~20% of float short.

[2026-08-27] Stock +20.5% to $227.96 (52-week high $229.08) on 23.4M shares; gave back ~4.5% on Aug 28 to ~$218. Q2 FCF $377M and OCF $530M; GAAP net income $5.3M vs a $70.2M year-ago loss.
[2026-08-24] Jefferies raised its target to $230 from $190 (Buy) into the print; CEO Kurtz called it the best quarter in company history, citing a ‘Mythos moment’ for AI-security demand.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 26 Q2 FY27 blowout: record $333M net-new ARR (+51%), $1.47B revenue, FY27 NNARR growth raised 630 bps to 34%.

[2026-08-19] BofA raised its NOW target to $150 from $130 (Buy). Stock remains ~25% below the $194.73 52-week high even after the two-day surge.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 27–28 SaaS re-rating after Salesforce’s blowout print; NOW had no earnings of its own this week.

down.name: DICKS SPORTING INC
down.company_description: Dick's Sporting Goods is a Consumer Discretionary specialty retailer of sporting goods, apparel and footwear; it also owns Foot Locker after a 2025 acquisition.
bullets: Aug 25 Q2: net sales $5.59B vs ~$5.64B Street; adj EPS $3.53 vs ~$3.76; namesake comps +4.9%, Foot Locker comps −3.6% with a ~$32M segment operating loss. Shares closed $124.31, −30.7% on ~38.5M shares.

FY26 non-GAAP EPS cut to $11.00–$12.00 from $13.50–$14.50; Foot Locker now guided to a $40–$80M full-year operating loss versus prior $110–$150M profit, while namesake comps outlook was held at +2.5% to +4%.

Consolidated FY sales guide $21.9–$22.2B (from $22.1–$22.4B); non-GAAP operating income ~$1.46–$1.56B. Management (Ed Stack) cited a more promotional athletic-footwear/apparel market and weak retro/legacy launches.
Foot Locker, acquired Sep 8 2025, contributed $1.74B of Q2 sales; Morningstar noted non-GAAP operating margin 7.9% vs 12.4% a year ago. 5d ~−26% vs SPX; 52-week high $244.38.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 25 Q2 miss and Foot Locker-driven FY EPS cut to $11–$12 from $13.50–$14.50 crushed the stock ~31%.

down.name: BURLINGTON STORES INC
down.company_description: Burlington Stores is a Consumer Discretionary off-price retailer of branded apparel, footwear, accessories and home goods across about 1,287 U.S. stores.
bullets: Aug 27 Q2: sales $3.00B (+11% YoY) missed ~$3.02–$3.03B; comps +2% vs +5% last year (7% two-year stack). Adj EPS $2.37 (+38%) beat ~$2.18–$2.19, excluding a $55M tariff-refund benefit.

Stock −7.6% Aug 27 then another ~−5.8% Aug 28 as Morgan Stanley cut its PT $438→$432. 5d ~−16%; 52-week high $378.33 (Jul 29).
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 27 Q2 sales miss, Q3 EPS $1.60–$1.70 vs ~$2.03, and a gas-price squeeze on core shoppers.

down.name: FERMI INC
down.company_description: Fermi is a Real Estate-classified developer of Project Matador, a Texas Panhandle private-power AI data-center campus that leases land and behind-the-meter generation.
bullets: Pre-revenue: Q2 (reported Aug 13) net loss $25.8M / $0.04 vs ~$0.06 Street; H1 loss $214.5M. Cash $91.7M at 6/30 before a July $431M 5.00% convertible due 2031 (conversion ~$9.52; capped-call effective $14.64).

No fresh print in the 5d window; shares ground from $5.92 (Aug 21) to ~$5.00 (Aug 28, −8.3% that day) vs a $36.99 52-week high. ~640M shares, ~$3.2B cap vs ~$17–$21 Street targets.

Aug 22 commentary framed the slide as digestion of a new CEO (Lee McIntire, Aug 11), wider losses, and convert dilution. COO RSU grant of 147k shares filed Aug 27; insiders sold >1M shares (~$7.3M) last quarter.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Post-Q2 digestion of convert dilution and pre-revenue AI-campus execution risk; shares slid to ~$5 vs a $37 high.

down.name: AST SPACEMOBILE INC CLASS A

bullets: No company print in the window. Q2 (Aug 10) revenue $31.5M vs ~$34M Street; GAAP EPS −$0.77 vs ~−$0.32, including a $125.9M involuntary-conversion charge on a lost BlueBird satellite. FY26 revenue guide $150–$200M.

down.ten_day_catalyst: High-beta, convert-funded satellite name sold off with space peers and rate-hike fears after Aug 24–28 macro news.

down.name: KARMAN HOLDINGS INC

Q2 (Aug 6, outside the window) was a beat: revenue $182.1M +58% (24% organic), adj EPS $0.14, adj EBITDA $54.6M (30% margin), backlog $1.3B; FY revenue raised to $730–$745M — so this 5d drop is not an earnings miss.
Multiple compression: ~$6.0–6.3B cap, ~169x TTM P/E; 52-week high $118.38 (Jan 29) vs ~$45.7 on Aug 28. Truist cut PT to $85 from $118 (~Aug 16); Evercore $100→$80.

down.ten_day_catalyst: Surprise Aug 26 CFO departure on top of multiple compression from a $118 high; no in-window earnings miss.

down.name: EVERPURE INC CLASS A

bullets: On Aug 26 Everpure reported Q2 FY27 (ended Aug 2) revenue of $1.19B, +38% YoY vs ~$1.10B consensus, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.70 vs $0.58; product revenue was $687M (+54%) and subscription $499M (+20%).

Shares still sold off: Aug 26 +5.9% to $108.90, then Aug 27 −8.9% to $99.24 and Aug 28 −5.9% to ~$93, ~22% below the Aug 18 52-week high of $119.10 — a sell-the-news fade after a ~40% early-August rally.

Quality of beat was mixed: free cash flow was −$238M (vs +$112M prior quarter), cash fell to ~$1.0B, and product GM stayed at the low end of the 65–70% range (68.4%); UBS kept Sell (PT $80 from $70) even as BofA upgraded to Buy ($150) and Morgan Stanley lifted its OW PT to $119.
See the wiki entry at wiki/companies/P (Everpure, formerly Pure Storage / PSTG).
down.ten_day_catalyst: Sell-the-news drop after a Q2 beat-and-raise; FCF turned negative and UBS kept Sell.

down.name: PAYPAL HOLDINGS INC
down.company_description: PayPal is a Financials-sector digital-payments firm that earns fees on branded checkout, Venmo, and Braintree merchant processing.
bullets: On Aug 28 PYPL closed $53.66, −12.7% on ~36M shares (more than 2× average) after Bloomberg reported Thursday night that Stripe and Advent International had abandoned a ~$60.50/share (~$53B) takeover bid.

The stock had rallied ~30% since mid-July bid reports and closed $61.47 on Aug 27, slightly above the rejected offer; PayPal’s board had called $60.50 insufficient and flagged financing/regulatory hurdles.
The collapse unwound the summer premium: PYPL had been ~$47 before the July leak (52-week low $38.46) and was the S&P 500’s largest decliner on Aug 28 even as the index rose.

Standalone fundamentals were already mixed: Q2 (Jul 28) revenue $8.68B (+5%) and TPV $486.4B (+10%) beat, with FY non-GAAP EPS raised to ~$5.38 and TM$ to ~$15.6B, but branded checkout TPV is only +2% FXN, Q3 EPS was guided to a low-single-digit decline, and international revenue fell 3% FXN.
See the wiki entry at wiki/companies/PYPL.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Stripe and Advent abandoned a $60.50/share takeover bid, wiping out the July premium.

down.name: TEMPUS AI INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Tempus AI is a Health Care-sector genomics and AI-diagnostics company selling NGS testing and analytics on clinical and molecular data.
bullets: The 5d drop is a fade of last week’s spike: TEM closed $72.69 on Aug 21 (intraday high $72.96) after +24.1% on Aug 19 on Merck/Moderna’s Phase 3 INTerpath-001 melanoma win, then fell to ~$64 on Aug 28 (−11.9% from the Friday close, −9.4% that day).

The Merck/Moderna readout was treated as validation of Tempus’s pending ~$1.5B Personalis MRD deal; BTIG raised its PT to $80 from $70 on Aug 20, but Street average targets (~$63) sat below the post-rally print.

Q2 (Jul 30) already showed first GAAP profit ($5.6M) on $382.5M revenue (+22%) and FY26 revenue guidance of $1.595–$1.605B, but TTM net income is still −$254M; Cathie Wood sold ~$4M of TEM around Aug 27 and CEO Fukushima sold 14,286 shares, adding to the unwind of a ~75% rally off the late-July ~$41.55 low.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Profit-taking after a Merck/Moderna-driven 75% rally; shares fell 9.4% on Aug 28.

down.name: MURPHY USA INC
down.company_description: Murphy USA is a Consumer Discretionary fuel-and-convenience retailer operating 1,700+ Walmart-adjacent and standalone stores across 27 U.S. states.
bullets: MUSA slid from $569.72 on Aug 21 to ~$504 on Aug 28 (−11.6%), with the damage clustered in three sessions: Aug 25 −4.2%, Aug 26 −2.3%, Aug 27 −4.2%.

On Aug 25 Brent fell 3.9% to ~$88.58 after the U.S. stopped short of penalizing China, the largest buyer of Iranian crude; energy-adjacent retailers de-rated with crude even though lower pump prices can later expand retail fuel margins.

The tape is still digesting the Aug 5 Q2 print: EPS $11.27 vs $9.95, revenue $6.81B (+36%), total fuel contribution 40.6 cpg vs 32.0 a year earlier, and adj. EBITDA $377.3M vs $286M — yet the stock fell ~9% after hours because H2 all-in fuel margins were assumed at 35 cpg (FY NI ~$636M / adj. EBITDA ~$1.25B).

Valuation compressed (Trefis: P/E ~23× in late April to ~15× by Aug 27) from the Jul 20 close high of $622 and 52-week high $636; the Aug 24 ex-div ($0.65, +1.6% raise) and Aug 20 White Castle autonomous-kiosk pilot were not the drivers.
down.ten_day_catalyst: H2 fuel-margin fade (35 vs 40.6 cpg in Q2) re-priced as crude fell on Aug 25.

down.name: ROCKET LAB CORP
down.company_description: Rocket Lab is an Industrials-sector space company selling Electron launches and satellites and pursuing an $8 billion Iridium acquisition.
bullets: RKLB fell from $72.57 on Aug 21 to ~$64.4 on Aug 28 (−11.3%), including Aug 24 −5.9% and Aug 28 about −5%; that extends a seven-session slide into Aug 27 of −19.4% that erased ~$10B of market value while the S&P 500 was roughly flat.

On Aug 27 SpaceX asked the FCC to scrutinize Iridium’s ‘anticompetitive’ conduct in the review of Rocket Lab’s ~$8B Iridium deal (shareholder vote Sep 24, close mid-2027), citing spectrum interference in the 19.4–19.6 and 29.1–29.3 GHz bands; SpaceX said it does not formally oppose the deal.

The derating started with the Aug 10 Q2 print: record revenue $234M (+62%, beat ~$231M) and backlog $2.36B (+137%), but EPS −$0.08 vs −$0.05 expected and FCF −$110M; Neutron’s debut has slipped toward late 2026/2027 after a Stage 1 tank rupture, and a ~$1.94B equity program hangs over the Iridium financing.

Even after the slide RKLB still trades ~51× trailing sales at a ~$40B cap, ~57% below the May 52-week high of $151, as SpaceX’s public listing repriced unprofitable space peers; Electron’s 93rd launch this week did not stabilize the stock.
down.ten_day_catalyst: SpaceX asked the FCC to scrutinize the $8bn Iridium deal during a 19% seven-session slide.

up.name: MODERNA INC
up.company_description: Moderna is a Health Care mRNA biotech that commercializes vaccines (COVID, RSV, flu) and develops personalized cancer therapies with Merck.
bullets: On Aug 19, Merck and Moderna said Phase 3 INTerpath-001 (1,137 patients) of intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940) plus KEYTRUDA met RFS and DMFS vs KEYTRUDA alone in resected stage IIB–IV melanoma — the first positive Phase 3 for an mRNA cancer therapy. Investopedia: MRNA +177% that day; BioPharma Dive: ~$45B of market value added; MRK also rose (Investopedia ~12%).

On Aug 5 the FDA approved mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010) for adults 50+, the first mRNA seasonal-flu vaccine and Moderna’s fifth product (fourth FDA). Supply is slated for the 2026–27 season; ≥65 approval is accelerated pending a postmarketing study.

The Phase 3 readout builds on KEYNOTE-942 5-year ASCO 2026 data: 49% lower risk of recurrence or death (HR 0.51) and 59% lower distant-metastasis risk (HR 0.41) vs KEYTRUDA alone. The companies will file with regulators; OS is still immature.
Health Care returned +7.3% vs SPY +3.5% over the 20d window; MRNA’s +137% is almost entirely the cancer-trial day plus the earlier flu approval, not a sector beta move.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 19 Phase 3 melanoma-vaccine win with Merck more than doubled the stock; Aug 5 FDA approved mRNA flu.

up.name: ATLASSIAN CORP CLASS A
up.company_description: Atlassian is an IT-sector collaboration-software company selling Jira, Confluence and JSM Cloud and Data Center subscriptions to 350,000-plus customers.
bullets: After the close 6 Aug 2026, TEAM reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $1.766B (+28% YoY) vs ~$1.66B consensus and non-GAAP EPS of $1.87 vs ~$1.50; Cloud was $1.213B (+31%), Subscription ARR $6.606B (+23%), RPO $4.817B (+44%).
Shares gapped ~35% on 7 Aug (close $110.17 on 6 Aug to an intraday high of $153.20), reversing a summer $80–$100 range after a SaaS-pocalypse drawdown.
FY27 guide: total revenue +13%, Cloud +25.5%, Subscription ARR +18%, Data Center −17%, non-GAAP OM ~25%; Q1 FY27 revenue $1.705–$1.715B with Cloud +28.5%. FY26 full-year revenue was $6.572B (+26%).
MCP server and Teamwork Graph CLI hit 1M MAU (more than doubled in one quarter); CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes disclosed a 10b5-1 plan to buy up to $250M of Class A stock.
See the wiki entry for Cloud/Data Center mix, Rovo, Atlassian Ascend and prior FY26 quarters.
up.ten_day_catalyst: 6 Aug Q4 beat-and-raise: $1.77B revenue, 31% Cloud growth; stock gapped ~35% 7 Aug.

up.name: NIQ GLOBAL INTELLIGENCE PLC
up.company_description: NIQ Global Intelligence is a Communication-sector consumer-intelligence company selling retail-measurement data and activation analytics to CPG brands and retailers.
bullets: After the close 10 Aug 2026, NIQ reported Q2 revenue $1,124.2M (+8.0% YoY; +5.8% organic CC) vs ~$1.12B Street, adjusted EPS $0.27 vs ~$0.20, and adjusted EBITDA $261.9M (+21.9%) with margin 23.3% (+270 bps).
Intelligence revenue $905.3M (+7.6% / +5.7% OCC); Activation $218.9M (+9.9% / +6.1% OCC). CEO Jim Peck: fifth consecutive quarter exceeding the top end of guidance on all key metrics.

Raised FY26: reported rev growth 7.1–7.4%, organic CC 5.2–5.6%, adj. EBITDA +15–17% and margin 23.5–23.9%, adj. EPS $1.08–$1.12 (from $0.95–$0.99). Levered FCF swung to +$74.1M (+$137M YoY); net leverage 3.1x.
Stock jumped 42% on 11 Aug, closing $16.58 — most of the 20-day +58.7% move — after a June low near $9.35.
up.ten_day_catalyst: 10 Aug Q2 beat-and-raise (adj. EPS $0.27, fifth top-end beat) sparked a 42% gap.

up.name: CARIS LIFE SCIENCES INC
up.company_description: Caris Life Sciences is a Health Care diagnostics company that sells molecular profiling and oncology tests using whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing.
bullets: On Aug 5 Caris reported Q2 revenue of $263.7M, +45% YoY, with molecular-profiling services at $252.3M (+55%) on ~59,200 clinical cases (+18% YoY), including ~48,300 MI Profile and ~10,700 Caris Assure cases.
The P&L inflected: net loss narrowed to $0.6M from $71.8M a year earlier, adjusted EBITDA was +$55.7M, operating cash flow $28.5M, free cash flow $6.4M, and gross margin 68% (+~500 bps YoY).

Management raised FY26 revenue guidance to $1.03–$1.04B (27–28% growth) from $1.00–$1.02B and reaffirmed ~20% clinical therapy-selection volume growth. QuiverQuant: shares +17.9% on Aug 6 after the print.

Operating highlights in the same release: Caris Detect multi-cancer early-detection blood test launched, MolDX approval for ChromoSeq myeloid whole-genome profiling, and a $100M buyback with ~$82.1M remaining. Health Care +7.3% vs CAI +60% over the window.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 5 Q2 beat-and-raise: $264M revenue (+45%) and FY26 guide lifted to $1.03–$1.04B.

up.name: ELASTIC NV
up.company_description: Elastic N.V. is an Information Technology search-AI software vendor selling Elasticsearch subscriptions for search, observability, and security.
bullets: On 2026-08-28 ESTC closed ~$99.91 (+19.3% day; +51.9% from the 2026-07-31 close of $65.79) after FY27 Q1 (ended 2026-07-31) beat-and-raise: revenue $478M (+15% YoY) vs ~$470M consensus; non-GAAP EPS $0.70 vs ~$0.58; sales-led subscription $399M (+18%); cRPO $1.153B (+21%); non-GAAP operating margin 16.2% vs ~14% guided.

FY27 guide was lifted to revenue $1.998–$2.010B and Q2 revenue $486–$487M (~15% YoY) with non-GAAP EPS $0.80–$0.82; mgmt cited record net adds to the >$100k ACV cohort and said 37% of those customers now run AI workloads vs ~21% a year earlier.

The print capped a pre-earnings grind: +7.4% on 2026-08-07 and +11.5% on 2026-08-13 as software caught a bid. Window catalysts also included a 2026-07-30 OpenAI collab (agents + GPT-5.5 Cyber in Elastic Security) and close of the Deductive AI observability deal on 2026-08-24.
Q1 absorbed $19.9M of the June 7% workforce-cut charges ($22–$25M total); Baird later lifted its PT to $120. See the wiki entry at wiki/companies/ESTC/.
up.ten_day_catalyst: FY27 Q1 beat-and-raise: $478M revenue, $0.70 adj. EPS, record large-customer adds.

up.name: PALANTIR TECHNOLOGIES INC CLASS A
up.company_description: Palantir is an Information Technology software company that sells AIP, Foundry, and Gotham platforms to U.S. government and commercial customers.
bullets: On 2026-08-04 PLTR jumped +29.5% to $162.66 on 173M shares after Q2 (reported 2026-08-03 AMC): revenue $1.94B (+93% YoY) vs ~$1.80B; adj. EPS $0.41 vs $0.35; GAAP NI $1.06B (55% margin); adj. operating margin 62%.

U.S. commercial revenue hit $764M (+149% YoY, +28% QoQ) with record $2.13B U.S. commercial TCV (+153%); U.S. government $809M (+90%). FY26 revenue guide raised to $8.15–$8.158B from $7.65–$7.66B; U.S. commercial FY now >$3.424B (≥134% growth).

Follow-through: +10.3% on 2026-08-07 to $172.01, then a grind to ~$186 by 2026-08-28 (~+51% from the 2026-07-31 close of $123.06). CEO Karp called the quarter “otherworldly” and tied demand to AI sovereignty vs frontier labs.
See the wiki entry at wiki/companies/PLTR/ (Q1 2026 US commercial was already +133% to $595M; this print accelerated that trajectory).
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q2 blowout: revenue +93% to $1.94B, U.S. commercial +149%; FY guide to $8.15B.

up.name: BULLISH
up.company_description: Bullish is a Financials-sector institutional crypto exchange (NYSE: BLSH) that provides digital-asset trading, liquidity, and CoinDesk data/media services.
bullets: Listing confirmed: NYSE BLSH since the 2025-08-13 IPO ($37; CEO Tom Farley, former NYSE president — not Fundstrat’s Tom Lee; Peter Thiel/Block.one-backed). The 20d bounce started at a 52-week low of $20.55 on 2026-07-31 (close $21.79) and ended ~$32–$33 (~+51%).

On 2026-08-13 Q2 mixed-but-better print: adj. revenue $92.6M (+62.5% YoY) vs ~$87.4M; adj. EBITDA $29.5M vs $8.1M a year ago; record subscription/services/other $62.7M offset $32.6B digital-asset sales (vs $58.6B). GAAP EPS −$1.78 missed; stock +11.6% then −11.2% on 2026-08-14.

Equiniti $4.2B deal remains on track for early-2027 close (HSR/CMA/Germany antitrust cleared); GFSC approved secondary trading of issuer-sponsored tokenized securities. FY26 SS&O guide refined to $225–$245M.

Second-leg rally 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-21 (+9.3%/+5.7%/+6.9%) tracked a bitcoin bounce (BTC ~+26% over 1m). On 2026-08-28 Bullish announced a $100M stablecoin debt facility to USD.AI for GPU financing.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Bounce from the Jul-31 52-week low on a Q2 adj.-revenue beat and Equiniti progress.

up.name: TEMPUS AI INC CLASS A
up.company_description: Tempus AI is a Health Care precision-medicine company selling genomic diagnostics and licensed multimodal data and AI models to clinicians and life-sciences firms.
bullets: 20d rally (not the late-August fade): TEM closed $43.87 on 2026-07-31 and peaked at $72.69 on 2026-08-21 before giving back to ~$64 on 2026-08-28 (−9.4% that day; still ~+46% over 20d). Q2 (2026-07-30): revenue $382.5M (+22% YoY) vs ~$380M; adj. EPS −$0.04 vs −$0.14; first GAAP profit $5.6M; adj. EBITDA $8.0M.

Guide raised to FY26 revenue $1.595–$1.605B and adj. EBITDA ~$65M. Oncology volume +31% YoY; MRD tests 9,000 vs 6,500 prior quarter; ~$200M of new data/applications licenses; $460M 0% converts due 2032.

On 2026-07-20 (just before the window) TEM agreed to buy Personalis for ~$1.5B EV ($16.25/sh). On 2026-08-19 TEM +24.1% after Merck/Moderna INTerpath-001 Phase 3 (intismeran autogene + Keytruda) hit RFS in resected melanoma — Personalis supplies the neoantigen sequencing — then +8.8%/+9.1% on 2026-08-20/21.

On 2026-08-24 FDA 510(k) cleared Tempus ECG-PH (AI pulmonary-hypertension screen on 12-lead ECGs). The last-week fade (−9.0% 2026-08-24, −9.4% 2026-08-28) is a giveback after a ~75% bounce from the late-July lows, not the 20d driver.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q2 beat-and-raise plus Merck-Moderna Phase 3 win validating the $1.5B Personalis deal.

up.name: PAYCOM SOFTWARE INC
up.company_description: Paycom is an Industrials-sector HCM software vendor that sells a single-database payroll, HR, and talent suite to mid-market employers on a recurring SaaS model.
bullets: Aug 5 Q2: revenue $531.2M (+9.8% YoY) beat by ~$18M; recurring/other $505.2M (+11.0%). GAAP EPS $2.34 vs $1.58 LY; non-GAAP EPS $2.78 vs ~$2.38 Street; adj. EBITDA $235M (44% margin).
Raised FY26: total revenue $2.197–2.212B (7–8% YoY) from $2.175–2.195B; recurring growth 8–9% (was 7–8%); adj. EBITDA $1.007–1.022B (~46% midpoint margin). Client-funds interest ~$105M.
Q2 capital return: 2.57M shares bought for $345.9M plus $17.9M dividends. H1 FCF $373M (33.8% margin). Cash $198M vs $900M long-term debt at Jun 30.
Print sparked a multi-day HCM rally (reports of ~6% to ~23% one-day pops depending on close); Simply Wall St later pegged the post-print move at +31% into Aug 9.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 5 Q2 beat ($531M, +11% recurring) and FY26 raise to $2.197–$2.212B drove a multi-day rally.

up.name: FIGURE TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS INC CL
up.company_description: Figure Technology Solutions is a Financials-sector blockchain capital-markets firm originating and tokenizing consumer loans, especially HELOCs, on Figure Connect.
bullets: Listing confirmed: Nasdaq FIGR (Class A; also tokenized as OPEN:FGRS). Shares ran from $24.91 on 2026-07-31 to the low-$36s by 2026-08-28 (~+45%), with +10.2% on 2026-08-12 and +13.8% on 2026-08-17 around earnings.

Q2 (reported 2026-08-13): Consumer Loan Marketplace volume $4.3B (+132% YoY, 4% above the high end of guide); Figure Connect $2.8B = 65% of volume (vs 56% prior qtr). Net revenue $226M (+113%); NI $87.4M (+192%, $0.35/sh); adj. EBITDA $119M at a 55% margin.

Added 102 origination partners to 489; weekly applications crossed $1B in July. Q3 CLM volume guided $4.8–$5.2B. Net take rate 3.6% (low end of 3.5–4%) as mix shifts to lower-take-rate Connect; mgmt now sees Connect approaching 70% of volume.

Kiavi acquisition still aimed at year-end (~40% volume add, ~$100M EBITDA). EDX Markets integrated Figure’s YLDS as collateral/treasury in the window — a small incremental RWA-tokenization print on top of the earnings re-rate.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q2 CLM volume $4.3B (+132%) and 55% adj. EBITDA margin as Connect hit 65%.

down.name: MONSTER BEVERAGE CORP
down.company_description: Monster Beverage is a Consumer Staples energy-drink maker that sells Monster, Reign, Bang and Coke-acquired brands worldwide, plus a small alcohol portfolio.
bullets: The −53% 20d / −49% 5d print is the Aug 11 2-for-1 split, not a collapse: new shares distributed after the Aug 10 close; unadjusted quotes halved (e.g. ~$91 prior close → $45.71 on Aug 11, −49.8%). Record date was July 24; sixth split since 2005. Market cap stayed ~$90B.

Aug 6 Q2 (pre-split) was a beat: net sales $2.54B (+20.2% YoY; +17.9% FX-neutral) vs ~$2.43B; GAAP EPS $0.59 / adj. $0.60 vs ~$0.58. Net income $584.5M (+19.6%). International sales $1.16B (+34.6%) reached 46% of the mix (from 41%).

Monster Energy drinks $2.36B (+21.6%); Strategic Brands $143.7M (+10.6%); Alcohol Brands $32.2M (−15.2%). Gross margin 55.9% vs 55.7%; opex 26.8% of sales (vs 25.8%) as selling spend rose to $269.2M from $196.9M.
No repurchase in Q2; ~$900M remained authorized as of Aug 5. Split-adjusted trading around $46 is consistent with the pre-split ~$91–$96 tape, so the Russell rank is a corporate-action artifact.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 11 2-for-1 split halved the unadjusted quote; Aug 6 Q2 was a beat, not a collapse.

down.name: LUCID GROUP INC
down.company_description: Lucid Group is a Consumer Discretionary EV manufacturer that sells luxury Air sedans and Gravity SUVs.
bullets: Aug 4 Q2: revenue $405M (+56% YoY) vs mixed Street (~$323–$416M); GAAP loss $3.30/sh vs ~$2.46–$2.72 expected after a $300M inventory impairment that cut gross margin ~74pp to −105%.

Produced 4,774 vehicles (−13% q/q) and delivered 3,953 (+19% YoY); CEO Silvio Napoli launched a $1.4B cash-flow reset, cut AMP-1 to one shift, delayed midsize Cosmos to late 2027, and withheld FY26 production/delivery guidance (2H production below consensus).
Aug 5 close $6.70 (−13.9% from $7.78) on 23.3M shares; stock then ground to ~$5.01 by Aug 28 as Q2 OCF burn hit $1.22B with $3.0B total liquidity and inventory $1.38B.

Earlier in the window: Jul 14 52-week low $2.37 on bankruptcy rumors, then a Jul 28 +21.5% spike that faded; Aug 28 largest-ever Air sedan fire-risk recall (more units than 2025 deliveries of 15,841).
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 4 Q2 miss, $300M inventory charge, and a production reset with no FY26 guide.

down.name: DICKS SPORTING INC
down.company_description: Dick's Sporting Goods is a Consumer Discretionary specialty retailer of sporting goods that also owns Foot Locker.
bullets: Aug 25 Q2 (13 weeks ended Aug 1): sales $5.59B vs $5.65B est; adj EPS $3.53 vs $3.76; namesake comps +4.9% (World Cup-aided) but Foot Locker comps −3.6% with ~$32M segment pretax loss.
FY26 adj EPS cut to $11–$12 from $13.50–$14.50 (~18% midpoint); Foot Locker comps now −2% to flat vs prior +1.5–3% growth, and FL operating profit flipped to a $40–$80M loss from $110–$150M profit.
Stock crashed 30.7% on Aug 25 (close $124.31 from $179.33) on ~38.5M shares; that 5d ~−26% wipeout is most of the 20d −31% from $195.91 on Jul 31.

Pre-print fade: Aug 20 close $179.34 (−6.3%) as legacy-sneaker weakness leaked; Ed Stack cited bloated industry inventory and shoppers “even more cautious… due to the geopolitical environment.” Nike/On slipped ~1.5–2.5% on the print.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 25 Q2 miss and Foot Locker guide cut that slashed FY26 EPS about 18%.

down.name: BURLINGTON STORES INC
down.company_description: Burlington Stores is a Consumer Discretionary off-price retailer of branded apparel, footwear, and home goods.
bullets: Aug 27 Q2: sales $3.00B (+11% YoY) missed ~$3.02–$3.03B; comps +2% vs +5% last year (7% two-year stack); adj EPS $2.37 (+38%) beat ~$2.18, excluding $55M of tariff refunds ($0.64/sh).
Stock fell 7.6% Aug 27 (close $290) then ~5.8% Aug 28 to ~$273; that 5d ~−16% is a large slice of the 20d −26% from the Jul 29 52-week high of $378.33.
Q3 adj EPS guided $1.60–$1.70 vs ~$2.03 Street; OM −80 to −60 bps as ~40% of refunds are reinvested in lower prices in Q3 and 60% in Q4 (full-year EPS impact called neutral).
FY adj EPS raised to $11.77–$11.97 (16–18% growth) and comps 3–4%, but CEO flagged July comp moderation and high gas prices squeezing core customers; 51 stores opened to 1,287.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 27 sales miss, soft Q3 EPS guide, and tariff refunds reinvested in price.

down.name: TRADE DESK INC CLASS A
down.company_description: The Trade Desk is a Communication Services adtech firm whose DSP lets advertisers buy programmatic display, video, and CTV ads.
bullets: Aug 6 Q2: revenue $715M (+3% YoY) missed ~$752M and the company’s own ≥$750M floor; adj EPS $0.34 vs ~$0.40–$0.41; adj EBITDA $241M at 34% vs 39% a year ago.
Q3 guide ≥$650M (~12% YoY decline vs ~$805–$840M Street) and adj EBITDA ~$160M (about half of year-ago $317M); CPG plus auto (~25% of spend) cited as pulling back.
Aug 6 close $17.67 (−6.8%), then Aug 7 crash −21.9% to $13.80 on 133M shares; 20d −25% from $18.04 on Jul 31, pinning near the $12.83 52-week low.
CEO Jeff Green said results were “below the standard we hold ourselves to,” blaming macro plus execution; Raymond James cut to Underperform. Kokai Zuma UI refresh announced Aug 27.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 6 Q2 miss and Q3 guide implying a roughly 12% revenue decline.

down.name: DAVITA INC
down.company_description: DaVita is a Health Care dialysis operator running U.S. and international outpatient kidney-care centers plus risk-based integrated-care contracts.
bullets: Aug 4 Q2: revenue $3.554B; diluted EPS $4.02 vs ~$3.88 Street (and $2.58 LY); operating income $579M (16.3% margin); FCF $256M. Bought 2.2M shares at $154.95 avg ($348M).
U.S. treatments 7.23M; per-day +1.09% seq / normalized non-acquired +0.3% YoY. Revenue per treatment $415.87, −$1.72 seq on weaker commercial/ACA mix and lower phosphate-binder revenue.
Reaffirmed FY26 adj. OI $2.15–$2.25B, adj. EPS $14.10–$15.20 (midpoint $14.65 vs ~$14.88 Street), FCF $1.00–$1.25B. Volume now expected near the top of +25–50 bps; H2 RPT slightly negative.
Call flagged a ~$40M 2026 commercial-mix headwind and ~$70M more in 2027 from ACA subsidy roll-off. Tape: ~6% to ~19% post-print drops depending on source as mix/RPT, not the EPS beat, set the price.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 4 EPS beat, but sequential RPT decline and FY midpoint below Street hit the stock hard.

down.name: DUTCH BROS INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Dutch Bros is a Consumer Discretionary drive-thru coffee chain selling handcrafted beverages through company-operated and franchised shops.
bullets: Aug 5 Q2: revenue $550.9M (+32.5% YoY) vs ~$525M Street; adj. EPS $0.33 vs $0.29; adj. EBITDA $113.7M (+27.8%) but margin −76 bps to 20.6%. Opened 48 shops (1,225 system at Jun 30).

Company-operated comps +8.3% (transactions +3.4% / ticket ~+4.9 pts); system comps +5.8% but system transactions only +1.7%. Management said H2 pricing adds <1 pt to ticket after a July increase rolled off.
Raised FY26: revenue $2.10–$2.13B, system comps 5–6% (trending midpoint), adj. EBITDA $385–$390M; capex lifted to $350–$370M, including a Phoenix franchise buy (~31 shops / $63.5M).
Stock fell ~16–19% Aug 6 (one tape to $53.33) as investors treated ticket-heavy comps, slower franchise traffic, and a bigger capex bill as the story, not the beat/raise.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 5 beat and FY raise, but ticket-heavy comps and a capex hike sent shares down ~19%.

down.name: UNDER ARMOUR INC CLASS C
down.company_description: Under Armour Class C is a Consumer Discretionary performance-apparel brand selling athletic clothing, footwear and accessories through wholesale and DTC.
bullets: Same company as UAA: Aug 7 Q1 FY27 (ended Jun 30) revenue $1.10B (−3%; −4% cc) vs ~$1.11B. NA −9% to $610M; international +5% to $490M (EMEA +12%, APAC −7%/−10% cc, LatAm +8%). Footwear −8%, eComm −12%, DTC −6%.

Gross margin 54.1% (+590 bps) almost entirely from IEEPA tariff refunds booked in FY26. GAAP EPS $0.00; adj. EPS $0.05. Op. income $47M / adj. $52M. Inventory $1.1B (−3%); cash $396M after retiring the 2026 notes.

FY27 revenue cut to a mid-single-digit decline from a prior “slight decline”: NA now MSD down (was LSD), APAC and EMEA now LSD down (were LSD up). Adj. operating income held at $140–160M and adj. EPS at $0.08–$0.12; GAAP LPS now $0.01–$0.05.

Shares had rallied ~30% into mid-July (~$7.43 on Jul 18). Print-day reaction was about −6% premarket / −7% session low / −4.5% EOD; the 20d −28.5% is that cut plus the pre-print rally unwinding into ~$5.25–$5.36.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 7 FY27 revenue-guide cut to a mid-single-digit decline unwound a pre-print rally.

down.name: UNDER ARMOUR INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Under Armour is a Consumer Discretionary athletic-apparel and footwear brand sold through wholesale and owned DTC channels.
bullets: Aug 7 Q1 FY27 (ended Jun 30): revenue $1.10B (−3% YoY) vs ~$1.11B; adj EPS $0.05 beat $0.02; North America −9% to $610M; APAC −7%; DTC −6% with e-commerce −12%.
FY27 revenue outlook cut to a mid-single-digit decline from a prior “slight” decline; NA now mid-single-digit down; APAC and EMEA flipped to low-single-digit declines from growth.
Profitability held: adj operating income still $140–$160M and adj EPS $0.08–$0.12; GM +590 bps to 54.1% on IEEPA tariff refunds; Q2 revenue guided to a high-single-digit decline.
Shares fell 5.3% Aug 6 then 4.5% Aug 7 and 9.0% Aug 11 (close $5.34); most of the 20d −24% from $6.65 on Jul 31 to ~$5.11 came in that post-print week.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 7 Q1 sales miss and FY27 revenue cut to a mid-single-digit decline.

down.name: REGAL REXNORD CORP
down.company_description: Regal Rexnord is an Industrials manufacturer of motion-control systems, industrial motors, and power-transmission components.
bullets: Aug 5 Q2: sales $1.558B (+4.2% YoY, +3.3% organic) missed ~$1.58B; adj EPS $2.99 beat $2.58 but included $0.39 of IEEPA tariff refunds; PES organic sales −6.6% on Resi-HVAC/pool/mining/ag.

FY26 adj EPS narrowed to $10.35–$10.85 with midpoint unchanged at $10.60, including $0.57 of refunds; FCF guide cut $50M to $600M; ex-refund EBITDA-margin outlook lowered on inflation, slower productivity, and mix.
Stock plunged 16.7% Aug 5 ($220.04 → $183.24) on 4.2M shares; Baird cut PT $300→$275 and KeyBanc to $240 on new CEO Aamir Paul’s first print.
Daily orders +8.8% (AMC +17.1%) and AMC organic sales +15.6% (data center, discrete automation, aero/defense) were not enough to offset the margin/FCF reset.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Aug 5 revenue miss and lower margin and FCF outlook despite an EPS beat.
